html:
The Awaswas, also called the Santa Cruz people, were a group of the Ohlone peoples of central California, living on the northern shore of Monterey Bay and in the Santa Cruz Mountains. They numbered perhaps 600 to 1,400, in small local groups, and their ancestors had lived in the area for thousands of years.

They gathered acorns, fished, collected shellfish on the coast and burned the land to keep meadows open. In 1791 Spain founded Mission Santa Cruz, one of the Spanish missions in California. The Awaswas were brought into the mission, where disease and harsh conditions killed most of them within a few decades. Neighbours: Mutsun and Ramaytush.
